unit.title: Ask it, or say “not”
unit.blurb: Turn a statement into a question, or into “not”
unit.intro: Two more changes you will use all the time. To ask a yes/no question, add _-ne_ to the first word: _Edis pānem_ (you eat bread) becomes _Edisne pānem?_ (do you eat bread?). To say “not”, put _nōn_ right before the verb: _Pānem nōn edis_ (you do not eat bread). Press **Run the drill** when you have met most of them.

roles.o: it is the object (the thing acted on), so it stays accusative

changes.label: Make it a question
changes.explain: _-ne_ on the first word turns a statement into a yes/no question: _{v}ne_. Nothing else changes.

foilsExtra.why: Without _-ne_ this is still a statement. Add _-ne_ to the first word to ask: _{v}ne_.

changes.label: Say you do not
changes.explain: _nōn_ means “not” and goes right before the verb: _nōn {v}_.

foilsExtra.why: _nōn_ goes before the verb it negates: _nōn {v}_.
That is the sentence you were given, with no “not”. To negate, put _nōn_ before the verb: _nōn {v}_.
